issues.title: [V1] Freeze gateway routes, trusted identity and message contracts
acceptance: Version the two API/event contracts and public `/api/media/*` / `/api/processing/*` paths; Gateway preserves these paths and each adapter strips its owner prefix exactly once.

Specify existing cookie/JWT/bcrypt login plus a Media-owned authorizer/current-role lookup; public identity headers are ignored, Processing never receives Media DB credentials, and public raw-source job creation is refused.
Define idempotent direct-S3 reservation/finalize and command/work/result envelopes with owner/source/attempt/version/tombstone rules; no media bytes, secrets or expiring URLs in SQS.

Contract fixtures cover malformed/expired/forged actors, wrong owner, replay, reorder and cancel-before-submit; document the worker project-source GET permission change and closed-session queued behavior.

Freeze producer permissions: only Media emits commands, Processing dispatch emits work and Processing completion emits results; consumers bind owner/asset/source revision to durable accepted state before source GET. Public API roles cannot inject raw-source work.
issues.files: docs/execution/interfaces.md; media/schemas; processing/schemas; existing public/private OpenAPI; new V1 contract fixtures

issues.title: [V1] Package Media Lambda with native credentials and owned SQL
acceptance: Run the existing Media application through an HTTP API payload-v2 adapter with correct path/cookie/error behavior; retain frontend behavior and basic login.
Add native Lambda S3 credentials/signing without ECS metadata/profile fallback; scoped role access, bounded grant expiry and credential-refresh tests.
Use invocation-scoped owned SQL connections and TLS; authorizer/runtime/migration roles stay distinct where needed and neither accesses processing_db.
Expose service/version health and independently version Media API/authorizer/result-handler artifacts; meaningful local Lambda-event and PostgreSQL checks pass.
issues.files: media/main.py; media/database.py; media/storage_credentials.py; media/api; deploy/media.Dockerfile; tests/media

issues.title: [V1] Package Processing Lambda API and owned job lifecycle
acceptance: Expose a separately deployed/versioned Processing API for owned job operations; trust verified Gateway context, reject forged public source creation and preserve retry/cancel semantics.
Keep jobs/attempts/leases in processing_db with owner-only migrations, invocation-scoped TLS connections and no Media ORM/settings/database import.
Separate API/control/worker privileges and entrypoints; FFmpeg never executes inside an API request.
Local payload-v2/authentication, PostgreSQL isolation, lifecycle and malformed-input checks pass; packaging is an implemented adapter, not only a template.
issues.files: processing/main.py; processing/auth.py; processing/database.py; processing/lifecycle.py; deployment handlers; tests/processing

issues.title: [V1] Replace Redis/RQ delivery with SQS and durable SQL repair
acceptance: Implement command/work/result SQS adapters with distinct consumers, matching DLQ/redrive policy, visibility renewal and bounded long polling.
Replace RQ job IDs, started registries, transport locks and Redis worker receipts with stable IDs and authoritative SQL state; no Redis/RQ imports or URL requirement in V1 runtime artifacts.
Commit outbox/inbox and domain state correctly; delete messages only after durable commit, with bounded retry/replay after lost send/delete responses and retention gaps.

Exercise duplicate/reordered work, publication failure, consumer restart, poison messages and stale attempt claims using an explicitly identified emulator/fake plus real PostgreSQL where state matters.

Enforce the contract producer/consumer allowlist in queue adapters and reject owner/source/job mismatches before encoding; cover injected messages and cross-owner source substitution with negative checks.
issues.files: processing/queue.py; processing/models.py; queue settings; worker queue entry; owned migrations; tests/processing

issues.title: [V1] Replace peer calls with commands, results and owned projections
acceptance: Media commits source/job intents and publishes trusted Processing commands; Processing deduplicates them and publishes versioned results from its owned outbox.
Media consumes results into an owned status/output projection; no synchronous per-request status peer call or worker source-grant callback remains in the V1 workflow.
Public status clearly distinguishes accepted/queued/processing/terminal state and handles a temporarily offline peer without fabricated completion.
Prove lost replies, duplicate and stale terminal events, deleted assets, cancel-before-submit and stored-source retry cannot revive or cross-own data.
issues.files: media/services/lifecycle.py; media/services/processing_client.py; media/models.py; Processing command/result handlers; both owned migrations

issues.title: [V1] Move browser and Publisher uploads directly to authorized S3
acceptance: Implement reserve/grant/upload/finalize for both clients while preserving the frontend design and public asset identity; no 100-MiB body crosses Gateway/Lambda.

Server generates owner-scoped keys and verifies the actual object size/content/checksum/revision before adoption; finalize/retry remains idempotent. Pin a server-verified immutable version/revision so replaying an upload grant cannot replace accepted bytes.
Reject forged key/owner, altered/missing/oversized objects, expired grants and abandoned/late finalization; retain orphan/uncertain-write cleanup.
Exercise browser CORS/cookies, Publisher HTTP-only independence and successful upload/edit/retry/playback/delete with normal TLS or the explicit local test CA.
issues.files: frontend/app.js; frontend tests; publisher; media/api/uploads.py; media/services/intake.py; media/services/storage.py

issues.title: [V1] Run finite SQS Fargate encoders and remove source callbacks
acceptance: Reuse the existing pure media engine for one attempt at a time, consuming SQS work and reading only its owned SQL state.

Use a scoped native ECS project-source GET role and output PUT role, verify immutable source identity/digest, and remove reverse Media source-grant HTTP calls. Resolve the descriptor from the durable accepted command/job; reject a substituted existing key belonging to another owner before GET/encode.
Preserve attempt lease/heartbeat/fencing, a finite absolute runtime, visibility renewal, graceful drain, forced-stop accounting and stored-source retry.

Adapt bounded operator batches/journal to SQS/SQL observations: maximum three nonterminal/reserved tasks, ambiguous launch replay uses the same token, zero idle workers. No unattended controller is implied.
issues.files: processing/worker; processing/lifecycle.py; scripts/aws/operations.py; worker Docker entry; tests/aws and worker integration

issues.title: [V1] Implement bounded Lambda repair and late-output cleanup
acceptance: Implement bounded owned recovery handlers for expired leases, stranded outboxes and stale output cleanup, reusing the tested durable lifecycle rules.
Handle ECS terminal events and late S3 output writes idempotently; cancelled/deleted/stale attempts cannot publish valid results or retain late private outputs unnoticed.
Use a session-scoped repair tick/continuation for gaps that events alone cannot cover; disable schedules/mappings during close and retain SQL repair state.
Test real owned SQL state plus selected event/emulator adapters for crash-before-send, lost ACK, late writes, retry races and a peer outage. Report real AWS delivery latency as NOT_RUN.

Preserve the original recovery gates in controlled local checks: lost committed queue work is re-enqueued within 120 seconds and interrupted work is requeued or marked failed within 300 seconds. A retry encode may await another explicit operator batch; no unattended launch is promised.
issues.files: media/recovery.py; processing/recovery.py; cleanup intents; Lambda event handlers; recovery tests

issues.title: [V1] Define managed Gateway/Lambda/SQS/Aurora infrastructure offline
acceptance: Render inert versioned definitions for two domain Lambda releases, owned authorizer, explicit routes, three queues/DLQs, private buckets, Aurora owner databases and native scoped roles/parameters.
Use the selected managed HTTPS legs; no V1 application EC2/nginx/Redis, NAT, paid endpoints, ALB or unselected Batch dependency. Validate database subnet/version/capacity assumptions.

Define invocation-scoped concurrency and permissions, required dual-stack service endpoints/S3 gateway route, owning migrations and bounded worker task definitions. Restrict each queue producer/consumer to its owning handler role; public API roles cannot publish raw-source work.
Schema/lint/policy/renderer checks pass with dummy inputs. No account calls, credential discovery, deployment or spend; produce a concrete future live-verification checklist.
issues.files: new deploy/aws/v1 definitions; scripts/aws adapters; role/SSM references; CloudFormation renderer checks

issues.title: [V1] Adapt independent releases, migrations and rollback to Lambda/Fargate
acceptance: Promote exact tested/scanned owner artifacts, Lambda versions/aliases and worker definitions using per-owner migration and compatibility gates.
Processing promotion/failed candidate restore keeps Media alias, image, roles/config and schema unchanged; Media promotion likewise preserves Processing.
Retain previous known-good artifacts, validate deployed candidates through the new public contracts and distinguish image rollback from schema rollback.
Locally verify adapter behavior, negative artifact/smoke cases and meaningful real service/SQL behavior; actual AWS version/runtime/clock receipts remain #65.
issues.files: scripts/aws/releases.py; artifacts.py; owner workflows; migrations; existing release tests

issues.title: [V1] Adapt session open/close, cost model and evidence protocols
acceptance: Open restores bounded function concurrency, queue mappings and repair schedules, waits for readiness, and permits explicit finite worker batches.

Close quiesces intake, drains/records terminal work, disables mappings/schedules and sets application/authorizer concurrency to zero; report eventual DB pause and possible maintenance/storage/request charges.

Replace ECS-core/state-host assumptions in target operations and forecast. Price actual DB-awake time, Lambda, SQS polls, pulls/retries/migrations, independent Fargate generator and retained data under the approximately $200 envelope.
Update safe evidence/job-input/restore/close handoffs. Local checks are distinct from #45 account authorization and #67 actual billing/pause/teardown proof.
issues.files: scripts/aws/operations.py; config.py; evidence.py; V1 cost calculator; job input template and runbook

issues.title: [V1] Verify the complete Redis-free workflow locally
acceptance: Run one coherent isolated browser + Publisher workflow with real PostgreSQL, real short encoding and explicit S3/SQS/Gateway/Lambda emulation boundaries.
Cover direct intake, normal identity/ownership, projection, edit, stored retry, MP4/HLS/range playback, delete, duplicate/reorder/cancel/late-write failures and finite close/wake.
Exercise independent owner promotion/failed rollback and cross-database/role negatives; no Redis/RQ in default V1 runtime or images. Preserve isolated legacy regression evidence/fixtures.
Provide an implemented V1 verification command in CI/runbook with source/digest evidence. Preserve historical thresholds/results; do not call emulated AWS identity/networking a cloud PASS.
issues.files: new V1 local runtime/verification entry; frontend/Publisher/real integration tests; CI and evidence manifest

issues.title: [V1] Record actual project account, currency and scoped cloud authorization
acceptance: Retain a nonsecret actual project account/region, operator, billing currency, available quota and resource/session ownership receipt; no credentials or other-project access.
Record the user approximately $200 envelope and chosen live limits with the actual currency. The V1 USD forecast is not an account bill or live-action authorization.
Record the approved resource/window/close/optional-deletion scope before any real AWS execution; local planning and implementation may progress without this receipt.
issues.files: private account/config inputs; public nonsecret authorization receipt

issues.title: [V1 decision] Replace the public EC2 HTTP origin with managed HTTPS
acceptance: Owner-selected V1 uses CloudFront HTTPS, API Gateway HTTPS origin and native Lambda integration; frontend and signed S3 object access use regional HTTPS. No public EC2 HTTP origin remains in the target.
Record generated service hostnames/certificate responsibility and private DB TLS in architecture-plan.md; no purchased domain, self-signed public certificate or hidden ALB/NAT.
Merge this reviewed decision into Main, then close this decision ticket only. Actual normal-trust browser/CLI and negative ingress receipts remain #63/#66.
issues.files: docs/execution/aws/architecture-plan.md; native AWS API Gateway/Lambda/CloudFront documentation

issues.title: [V1 evidence] Deploy the approved target and prove real workflow boundaries
acceptance: After actual account/scope authorization and all required local migrations, capture real Gateway routes, Lambda identities/versions, Aurora roles/TLS, SQS/DLQ permissions and S3 grant behavior.
Run short browser and Publisher reserve/upload/finalize/status/edit/retry/delete/playback checks through normal public TLS, including forged identity, wrong-owner and cross-database denials.

Verify native Lambda/ECS credentials and the selected worker source-GET/output-PUT/cleanup permissions; no secrets in evidence. Prove deployed V1 has no Redis/RQ/state-host dependency. Capture denied unauthorized queue sends and cross-owner source substitution against the deployed policies/consumers.

Retain real source/digests, executed versus NOT_RUN outcomes and actual endpoint/pause/readiness behavior. Keep the six long uploads for #64; short >5-MiB multipart may be checked here within the shared upload allowance.
issues.files: future authorized V1 deployment, client/role evidence and safe manifests

issues.title: [V1 evidence] Prove 1/2/3 encoders and bounded SQS recovery on AWS
acceptance: Capture ordinary 2-vCPU workers at fixed counts 1/2/3 with exactly 1/2/3 long submissions respectively: six long uploads total; record image, limits, actual task residency and outcomes.
Use short/stored sources for interruption, duplicate/lost delivery, cancelled/stale attempts, empty-burst and finite drain; confirm the global three-task reservation cap.
Distinguish capacity/recovery smoke from the historical full scaling target. Retain failed observations; do not rewrite original #38/#39 results or silently expand fixtures.

Record SQS/SQL repair and user-visible failure timing, real terminal outcomes and zero remaining encoders after drain, with selected safe receipts. Retain the original <=120-second lost-queue repair and <=300-second interrupted-job requeue/failure gates; do not equate operator-delayed execution with automatic starts.

issues.title: [V1 evidence] Capture independent Lambda/Fargate release and rollback
acceptance: Capture a real Processing good promotion and failed candidate restoration with exact Lambda aliases/versions and worker digests; Media aliases/artifacts/schema remain unchanged.
Capture Media owner promotion/rollback with unchanged Processing receipts, compatible owning migrations and current/rollback artifacts.
Run the same public/client smoke and clock the actual operation, including failures, startup and restoration; retain the original 600-second good-promotion/300-second bad-operation gates.
No successful image rollback is presented as reversal of a destructive migration or proof from local adapters alone.

issues.title: [V1 evidence] Measure warm API latency with an independent Fargate generator
acceptance: Run one serial eligible status cycle: 50 users/180 seconds, p90 <=700 ms and errors <1%; then 20-login cycle p90 <2 seconds, with unchanged password hash strength and explicit warmup.
Use a separate temporary Fargate generator/task definition, not an API/encoder/DB placement; retain configured CPU/RAM, source/digests, safe raw samples/hash/length and p90 arithmetic.
Record cold Lambda/Aurora wake separately; do not introduce retries in timed windows, suppress failures, tune in the evidence ticket or relabel local results.
Reuse assets, perform no new bulk upload, account for the priced generator task/IP lifetime and retain actual stopped-task receipts.

issues.title: [V1 evidence] Reconcile actual spend, close state and final V1 handoff
acceptance: Capture zero encoder/migration/generator tasks, disabled event mappings/repair schedules and zero application/authorizer reserved concurrency after drain; observe DB pause without hiding maintenance/request/storage charges.

Reconcile actual Lambda GB-seconds, Aurora ACU-awake/storage/I/O, SQS polls, Fargate pulling-to-stop, image/log/S3/CDN and later bill lines against the V1 model and actual account currency; absent billing remains pending.

If backup/restore is claimed, restore an authorized isolated coherent target and verify owner/reference/source consistency; otherwise state NOT_RUN and data-loss limits. Optional destructive cleanup still needs exact approved scope.

Keep original local evidence/latency/scaling gates intact, link #63–#66 receipts, and tag the immutable project2-v1 baseline only when all required V1 implementation/acceptance passes. This issue does not require V2.

issues.title: [V2 experiment] Benchmark bounded short encodes on Lambda
acceptance: Start from accepted immutable V1 and use the same pure engine and fixed short fixture; define admission, full-pipeline deadline/headroom, memory/scratch and combined executor-cap rules before implementation.
Compare cold/warm complete-job latency, correctness, interruption/retry, cleanup and actual cost per success with V1 Fargate; local 24-second medians are not Lambda evidence.
Merge only if a measured benefit justifies the additional execution path; preserve V1 and stop at the remaining time/spend limit. No V1 issue depends on this experiment.

issues.title: [V2 experiment] Measure separate database clusters and pause behavior
acceptance: Start from accepted V1; compare the single-cluster/two-owned-DB baseline with two independent clusters or a narrowly scoped pause/capacity change.
Measure isolation, connection/cold resume, warm latency, migration/restore/release behavior and real cost without changing the application database model.
Keep the V1 default unless evidence warrants the change. Data API/DSQL/DynamoDB requires a separately chosen compatibility spike, not an automatic expansion of this issue.

issues.title: [V2 experiment] Optional unattended worker starts and further cost cuts
acceptance: Remain outside the V1 critical path. First V1 demo uses serialized finite operator batches; a queued UI state is explicit.

After accepted V1, choose one measured automation/cost experiment. Unattended launch must preserve SQL coordination/reservations, stable launch tokens, cap including ambiguous requests, and close/release interlocks.

Prove no-backlog/no-launch, restart/lost-response/concurrent-trigger behavior, bounded three-executor cap and no idle respawn. Batch/Spot/ARM/consolidation are separate options, not a bundled programme.
